Rashi on Pesachim 67b:11:1.english: With regard to their impurity - That [he] is not impure [for] seven [days] like a zav or like one impure from a corpse.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:11:2.english: Impurity until evening is explicitly written about it - "When semen goes out from him, he shall bathe in water, etc." (Leviticus 15:16).

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:12:1.english: Just as a creeping animal imparts impurity through an accident - If a dead creeping animal fell upon him.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:12:2.english: Becomes ritually impure through an accident - For example, if he experienced [a seminal emission] due to an excess of food and drink.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:1:1.hebrew: זב נמי מטמא באונס - כגון בראיה ראשונה, שאין בה אלא טומאת ערב, דאיתקש לשכבת זרע, דכתיב (ויקרא ט״ו:ל״ב): "זאת תורת הזב ואשר תצא ממנו שכבת זרע", והיינו ראיה ראשונה, דלא מנה ביה בהאי קרא אלא חדא זיבה, דאזלינן בתר מניינא דקרא, כדאמרינן במגילה (ד' ח.): "מנה הכתוב שתים וקראו טמא" כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:1:1.english: A zav also becomes impure through an accident - For example, in [the case of] a first sighting, which involves only evening impurity, for it is juxtaposed [in Scripture] to a seminal emission, as it is written (Leviticus 15:32): "This is the law of the zav, and of him from whom semen goes out." And this refers to a first sighting, for in this verse [Scripture] counted only one discharge, since we follow the count [stated] in the verse, as we say in [Tractate] Megillah (8a): "Scripture counted two [sightings] and called him impure," etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:1:2.hebrew: מטמאה באונס - מהאי היקש גופיה נפקא ליה לרב הונא: מה קרי מטמא באונס — אם ראה מחמת רוב מאכל ומשתה, דגבי קרי לא כתיב מיעוטא — אף ראיה ראשונה של זב מטמאה באונס. זוב דומה ללובן ביצה המוזרת, שכבת זרע דומה ללובן ביצה שאינה מוזרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:1:2.english: Establishes impurity through an accident - Rav Huna derives [this] from this very juxtaposition: just as a seminal emission imparts impurity through an accident — if he experienced [an emission] due to excessive food or drink, for regarding a seminal emission no exclusion is written — so too the first sighting of a zav imparts impurity through an accident. Zov resembles the white of a spoiled egg; semen resembles the white of an egg that is not spoiled.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:2:1.english: Letting [the hair] grow - Letting the head [go unkempt, i.e.,] growing hair.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:2:3.hebrew: ואסור בתשמיש המטה - כדכתיב (ויקרא י״ד:ח׳) וישב מחוץ לאהלו, ואין אהלו אלא אשתו. למאן דאמר במועד קטן (ד' ז:) ק"ו לימי חלוטו, איכא חומרא טובא; ולמאן דאמר ימי ספרו דוקא, אפ"ה חומרא מיהא היא, דאילו זב לא מיתסר מידי בתשמיש:
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:2:3.english: And he is prohibited from marital relations - As it is written (Leviticus 14:8), "and he shall dwell outside his tent," and "his tent" means none other than his wife. According to the one who says in Moed Katan (7b) [that there is] an a fortiori inference to the days of his confirmed leprosy, there is a great stringency; and according to the one who says [it applies] specifically [to] the days of his counting, even so, it is nevertheless a stringency, whereas a zav is not prohibited from [marital] relations at all.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:2:4.hebrew: זב - עושה משכבו ומושבו אב הטומאה לטמא אדם הנוגע בו טומאה חמורה, לטמא בגדים שעליו, אע"פ שלא נגעו הבגדים במשכב. אבל מצורע, אע"ג דתניא בתורת כהנים עושה משכב ומושב, לאו אב הטומאה לטמא אדם לטמא בגדים, אלא לטמא אוכלין ומשקין:
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:2:4.english: A zav - He renders his couch and seat a primary source of impurity, to contaminate a person who touches it [with] severe impurity, to contaminate the garments upon him, even though the garments did not touch the couch. However, [regarding] a metzora, even though it is taught in Torat Kohanim [that he] renders a couch and seat [impure], [it is] not a primary source of impurity to contaminate a person [so as] to contaminate garments, rather [only] to contaminate foods and beverages.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:2:5.hebrew: ומטמא כלי חרס בהיסט - דכתיב (ויקרא ט״ו:י״ב): "וכלי חרס אשר יגע בו הזב ישבר". ותניא בתורת כהנים: יכול אפילו נגע בו הזב מאחוריו יהא טמא? תלמוד לומר "אשר יגע בו", ולהלן הוא אומר "אשר תבושל בו": מה "בו" האמור להלן מאוירו, אף "בו" האמור כאן אינו מטמא במגע אלא מאוירו. אם כן, מאחר שלמדנו שמטמא אותו מאוירו, מה ת"ל "אשר יגע בו"? פירוש: ומה חלק בו ומה הוסיף בו בכלי חרס בטומאת הזב מבשאר טומאות במגעו שהוא ככולו? הוי אומר: זה היסטו:
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:2:5.english: And he imparts ritual impurity to an earthenware vessel through movement - As it is written (Leviticus 15:12): "And an earthenware vessel that the zav touches shall be broken." And it is taught in Torat Kohanim: Could [one think that] even if the zav touched it from its back [i.e., its exterior], it would be impure? The verse states, "that [he] touches it [bo]," and elsewhere it says, "in which [bo] it is cooked" — just as "bo" stated there [refers to] its airspace, so too "bo" stated here [means] it does not contract impurity through [mere] contact, but rather through its airspace. If so, since we have learned that he imparts impurity to it through its airspace, why does the verse state, "that [he] touches it"? Explanation: What distinction did [Scripture] make and what did it add regarding an earthenware vessel in the impurity of a zav over other impurities, through a touch of his that is like [affecting] all of it? You must say: this is his moving [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:3:1.hebrew: ומשנינן זב וכל זב לרבות - קרי כזב. וכיון דאיתרבי בעל קרי לישתלח חוץ לשתי מחנות, לא איצטריך מצורע, דחמור מבעל קרי:
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:3:1.english: And we answer: “Zav, and any zav, to include” - [one who experienced] a seminal emission like a zav. And since one who experienced a seminal emission was included to be sent outside two camps, [a verse for] a leper is not needed, for he is more severe than one who experienced a seminal emission.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:4:1.hebrew: ופרכינן מאי חומרא כדאמרן - וכיון דלא איצטריך וכתביה רחמנא, ליתן לו מחנה שלישית. אדרבא כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:4:1.english: And we ask: What is [his] stringency? As we said - And since it was not needed, and [yet] the Merciful One wrote it, [it is] to give him a third camp. On the contrary, etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:4:2.hebrew: במשהו - כעין חרדל ובפחות מכאן, במסכת נדה (ד' מ:). ומצורע שיעורו כגריס, בתורת כהנים:
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:4:2.english: With any amount - Like a mustard seed, and [even] with less than that, in Tractate Niddah (40b). Whereas a leper, his [minimum] measure is the size of a split bean, [as stated] in Torat Kohanim.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:5:1.hebrew: כחתימת פי האמה - כדי סתימת נקב פי אמתו, ויליף לה מ"החתים בשרו את זובו" במסכת נדה (דף מג:):
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:5:1.english: Like a blockage of the tip of the organ - [Sufficient] to stop up the orifice at the tip of his organ, and he derives it from [the verse], "his flesh is stopped up [from] his discharge," in Tractate Niddah (43b).

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:5:2.hebrew: ואיתקש בעל קרי לזב - כדכתיב: "זאת תהיה תורת הזב ואשר תצא ממנו שכבת זרע", מה זב צריך כחתימת פי האמה, אף בעל קרי. אלמא מצורע חמור, דאזלא ליה פירכא דכל שהוא. וכי איצטריך קרא, ליתן לו מחנה שלישית:
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:5:2.english: And one who experienced a seminal emission is compared to a zav - As it is written: "This is the law of the zav, and of him from whom semen goes out" — just as a zav requires [a discharge sufficient for] the blockage of the tip of the [male] organ, so too [does] one who experienced a seminal emission. Thus, a leper is more stringent, for the refutation of [imparting impurity with] any minimal amount is removed. And when [the verse] is needed, [it is] to assign him a third camp.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:6:1.hebrew: וכל - דכתיב גבי מצורע, מאי (כל) מרבי גבי דין מצורע:
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:6:1.english: And any - that is written regarding a leper: what does ("any") include regarding the law of a leper?

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:7:1.hebrew: שפיר קאמר ר' שמעון - דמפיק ליה מההוא קרא דין שילוחין, ולמה לי קרא אחרינא:
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:7:1.english: Rabbi Shimon spoke well - For he derives the law of sending out [from the camps] from that verse, and why do I need another verse?

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:8:1.hebrew: ההוא - צרוע וזב, לכדר' אליעזר אתי, לאקשינהו לטמא מת, לפוטרו מן ההיכרת בפסח הבא בטומאה, ואע"ג דלא אישתרי להו לכתחלה בביאת מקדש:
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:8:1.english: That [verse] - [mentioning] a leper and a zav comes for [the teaching] of Rabbi Eliezer, to compare them to one impure due to a corpse, to exempt him from karet during a Paschal lamb that is brought in [a state of] impurity, even though entering the Temple is not permitted for them initially.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:8:2.hebrew: אין טמאי מתים משתלחין - כגון פסח הבא בטומאה, דאישתרו (טמאי מתים לכתחלה כשרוב הציבור טמאי מתים, כדכתיב איש וכו'), כדלעיל בשמעתין:
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:8:2.english: Those impure due to a corpse are not sent out - For example, [during] a Paschal lamb that is brought in [a state of] impurity, when they are permitted (those impure due to a corpse [are permitted] from the outset when the majority of the congregation are impure due to a corpse, as it is written: “Any man...,” etc.), as [stated] above in our discussion.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:8:3.hebrew: אין זבין ומצורעין משתלחין - שילוחן הראשון בכרת, ומיהו לכתחלה לא אישתרו, דהא טמא לנפש גלי רחמנא דאין ציבור נדחין, הא בשאר טומאות נדחין. מיהו אהני היקישא לפוטרן מן ההיכרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:8:3.english: Zavin and lepers are not sent out - Their primary sending out [carries the penalty of] karet, yet in the first place they are not permitted [to enter]; for [it is specifically regarding] one impure by a corpse [that] the Merciful One revealed that a community is not deferred, whereas with other impurities they are deferred. Nevertheless, the heikesh [scriptural analogy] is effective to exempt them from karet.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:9:1.hebrew: מחילות לא נתקדשו - הני תרתי מילי שמעינהו כי הדדי מרביה, וכי הדדי אמרינהו. מחילות ומערות שלתחת העזרה לא נתקדשו בקדושת עזרה:
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:9:1.english: The tunnels were not sanctified - These two statements he heard together from his teacher, and together he stated them. Tunnels and caves that are beneath the [Temple] Courtyard were not sanctified with the sanctity of the Courtyard.

Rashi on Pesachim 67b:9:2.hebrew: ובעל קרי משתלח כו' - והיינו כברייתא, דהא איתקש לזב:
Rashi on Pesachim 67b:9:2.english: And a person who experienced a seminal emission is sent out, etc. - And this is in accordance with the baraita, for he has been equated to a zav.

Tosafot on Pesachim 67b:1:1.hebrew: כי האי גוונא זב נמי טמויי מטמי באונס - תימה לרשב"א: אכתי שרץ חמור, שמטמא בכעדשה, מה שאין כן בזב, דכר' נתן מוקמ' לה דבעי חתימת פי האמה, דהוי טפי אפילו מכגריס, כדמוכח בסמוך. ואור"י דאם היו מפזרין העדשה יהיה יותר מחתימת פי האמה ומגריס; ודוחק. ונראה לתרץ, דאיכא למימר "טמא מת יוכיח", דבכזית. וכי פריך בסמוך "אדרבה, בעל קרי חמור שכן מטמא במשהו", לא שייך "טמא מת יוכיח", דהא אין משולח אלא חוץ למחנה אחת, ושם רוצה שיהא מצורע משתלח חוץ לשתי מחנות כבעל קרי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 67b:1:1.english: "In a case like this, a zav also becomes impure through an accident" - It is astonishing to the Rashba: Still, a creeping animal [sheretz] is more severe, as it imparts impurity in the size of a lentil, which is not the case with a zav, for we establish [the law of a zav] according to Rabbi Natan, who requires [enough discharge to] seal the opening of the organ, which is even more than the size of a split bean [k'gris], as is proven shortly. And Rabbi Yitzchak [R"I] says that if one were to spread out the lentil-[sized piece], it would be more than the sealing of the opening of the organ and [more than] a split bean; and [this] is forced. And it appears [possible] to answer that one can say: "One who is impure from a corpse proves [otherwise]," as [a corpse imparts impurity] in the size of an olive. And when [the Gemara] asks shortly, "On the contrary, one who experienced a seminal emission is more severe, as he imparts impurity with a minute amount [mashehu]," [the refutation] "one who is impure from a corpse proves [otherwise]" does not apply [there], because [one impure from a corpse] is only sent out of one camp, whereas there [the Gemara] wants a leper [metzora] to be sent out of two camps, like one who experienced a seminal emission.

Tosafot on Pesachim 67b:2:1.hebrew: שכן טעון פריעה ופרימה - תימה לר"י, אמאי לא קאמר נמי שכן מטמא בביאה, הבא אל האהל:
Tosafot on Pesachim 67b:2:1.english: "For [a leper] is required to let his hair grow and rend his garments" - It is astonishing to Rabbeinu Yitzchak: why does [the Gemara] not also say "for [he] imparts impurity through entering," [that is,] one who enters the tent?

Tosafot on Pesachim 67b:2:2.hebrew: ואסור בתשמיש המטה - כמאן דאמר בפ"ק דמ"ק (ד' ז:) דמוחלט אסור בתשמיש המטה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 67b:2:2.english: "And he is prohibited from marital relations" - [This is] in accordance with the one who says in the first chapter of Moed Katan (7b) that a confirmed [leper] is prohibited from marital relations:

Tosafot on Pesachim 67b:2:3.hebrew: שכן עושה משכב ומושב - פירש בקונטרס דהא דתניא בת"כ דמצורע עושה משכב ומושב, לא לטמא אדם ובגדים אלא לטמא אוכלין ומשקין. אבל ליכא למימר דהא מיירי במצורע בימי ספרו דאינו עושה משכב ומושב כדקתני בהדיא בת"כ, דהא אמר הכא דמשולח חוץ לג' מחנות, ובשילהי מסכת נגעים (פי"ד מ"ג) תנן דבימי ספרו הוי כטמא שרץ, אלמא אינו משולח אפי' חוץ למחנה לויה; והא דקתני נמי התם "ונכנס לפנים מן החומה" — לאו דוקא לפנים מן החומה. ועוד, דמסיק הכא: "שכן טעון פריעה ופרימה", והיינו במוחלט. והקשה הרב משה מפוטייש"א: דתניא בתורת כהני' (אשר ישכב): "איש אותה — פרט למצורעת"; ואי מצורע לא מטמא משכב ומושב, למ"ל למעוטי? מהיכי תיתי שתטמא את בועלה? דמנדה לא ילפא, שכן מטמאה משכב ומושב! אלא ודאי מטמאה משכב ומושב, להכי איצטריך קרא למעוטי. ויש לומר דאסמכתא בעלמא היא. ועוד הקשה מהא דאמר: "לזכר — לרבות מצורע למעיינותיו", אקשיה רחמנא לזב: מה זב ראייתו מטמא במשא כו', והואיל ואיתקיש, אין היקש למחצה, ולמשכב ומושב נמי איתקש! ולאו פירכא היא, דאם כן למחנותם נמי נימא דאיתקש, ואם כן מאי פריך הכא? והא דתנן בפרק בתרא דמסכת זבין (פ"ה מ"ו): "הנוגע בזב ובזבה במצורע כו' אחד הנוגע אחד המסיטו ואחד הנושא ואחד הנישא", אלמא משמע דמצורע מטמא בהיסט, ובשמעתין משמע דלא מטמא — אור"ת דהא דקתני "נישא", דמשמע דמטמא בהיסט, לא קאי אמצורע אלא אשארא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 67b:2:3.english: [For a zav] renders [what he] lies or sits on [impure] - Rashi explained that what is taught in Torat Kohanim — that a leper renders [what he] lies or sits on [impure] — is not to render a person and garments impure, but rather to render food and beverages impure. However, one cannot say that this [Gemara here] is speaking of a leper during his days of counting, when he does not render [what he] lies or sits on [impure], as is taught explicitly in Torat Kohanim, for [the Gemara] says here that he is sent outside the three camps, whereas at the end of Tractate Nega'im (14:3) we learned in a Mishnah that during his days of counting he is like one who is impure from a creeping animal, which proves he is not sent even outside the Camp of the Levites; and that which it also teaches there, "and he enters inside the wall," does not literally [mean] inside the wall. And furthermore, because [the Gemara] concludes here: "for he requires letting his hair grow and rending [his garments]," and that is [specifically] for a confirmed [leper]. And Rabbi Moshe of Pontoise raised a difficulty: For it is taught in Torat Kohanim (on "whoever lies"): "'a man [with] her' — this excludes a female leper [from imparting impurity to one who has relations with her]"; now, if a leper does not impart impurity to [what he] lies or sits on, why do I need [a verse] to exclude [her]? From where would we have thought that she imparts impurity to one who has relations with her? For she cannot be derived from a niddah, since [a niddah] imparts impurity to [what she] lies or sits on! Rather, she certainly imparts impurity to [what she] lies or sits on, and therefore a verse was needed to exclude [her]. And one can say that it is merely an asmakhta [a scriptural support]. And he raised a further difficulty from that which [the Sages] say: "'For a male' — to include a leper regarding his bodily emissions," [where] the Merciful One compared him by scriptural analogy (heikesh) to a zav: just as a zav's sighting imparts impurity through carrying, etc., and since he was compared by heikesh, there is no partial heikesh, so he should also be compared regarding [imparting impurity to what he] lies or sits on! But this is not a refutation, for if so, let us also say that he was compared regarding their camps, and if so, what does [the Gemara] ask here? And as for that which we learned in the Mishnah in the last chapter of Tractate Zavim (5:6): "One who touches a zav, or a zavah, or a leper, etc. — whether one touches [them], or one moves [them], or one carries [them], or one is carried [by them]," which implies that a leper imparts impurity through movement, whereas in our sugya it is implied that he does not impart impurity [through movement] — Rabbeinu Tam says that that which it teaches "one who is carried," which implies that he imparts impurity through movement, does not refer to the leper, but rather to the others [listed in that Mishnah]:

Tosafot on Pesachim 67b:5:1.hebrew: ואיתקש בעל קרי לזב - הכא משמע דבעל קרי נמי טמא מטעם ראיה, ואומר ר"י דפליגא אההיא דריש המפלת (נדה דף כב.), דקאמר התם: "בעא מיניה רבא מרב הונא: הרואה קרי בקיסם מהו? אמר ליה: ותיפוק ליה דהוא עצמו אינו מטמא אלא בחתימת פי האמה!", וקאמר: "למימרא דנוגע הוי?" — פירוש: מדבעי חתימת פי האמה, אלמא משמע התם דמטעם נגיעה טמא. ובפרק יוצא דופן (נדה דף מב.) דקאמר: "שכבת זרע לרואה במשהו, לנוגע בכעדשה" — פליגא אדשמעתא ודהמפלת:
Tosafot on Pesachim 67b:5:1.english: And one who experienced a seminal emission is compared to a zav - Here it implies that one who experiences a seminal emission is also ritually impure by reason of discharge. And R. Yitzchak says that [this] disagrees with that [passage] at the beginning of [the chapter] HaMapelet (Niddah 22a), where it says there: "Rava asked Rav Huna: One who experiences a seminal emission with a splinter, what is [the law]? He said to him: Let it follow that he himself only becomes impure with the blockage of the tip of the organ!" And [the Gemara] asks: "Is that to say that he is [considered] one who touches [semen]?" — meaning: since it requires the blockage of the tip of the organ, thus it implies there that he becomes impure by reason of touching. And in the chapter Yotzei Dofen (Niddah 42a), where it says: "Semen: for one who experiences a discharge, [it defiles] in any minute amount; for one who touches [it], [it defiles] in [an amount] the size of a lentil" — [that] disagrees with [our] sugya and with [the passage in] HaMapelet.

Tosafot on Pesachim 67b:9:1.hebrew: מחילות לא נתקדשו - וא"ת: הא אמר בפ"ב דזבחים (דף כד.): "נעקרה אבן ועמד במקומה, מהו?" כו', ומסיק: לעולם פשיטא ליה דכי קדיש דוד רצפה, עד ארעית תהומא קדיש. וי"ל דבכיצד צולין (לקמן פסחים דף פו.) מסקינן: כי א"ר יוחנן — בפתוחות לחול, אבל פתוחות לקודש — קודש:
Tosafot on Pesachim 67b:9:1.english: The tunnels were not sanctified - And if you ask: Behold, [the Gemara] says in the second chapter of Zevachim (24a): "If a stone was uprooted and he stood in its place, what is [the law]?" etc., and it concludes: Actually, it is obvious to him that when David sanctified the floor, he sanctified [it] down to the bottom of the abyss. And one can answer that in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin (later in Pesachim 86a) we conclude: When Rabbi Yochanan said [this], [it was] regarding [tunnels] that open to non-sacred space, whereas [tunnels] that open to sacred space are sacred.
